We investigate problems encountered in the analysis of longitudinal change, where the difference in some outcome variable is modeled on a set of regressor variables in a linear regression model. Previous work demonstrated the effects of measurement error in the analysis of change in wall thickness of the common carotid artery, showing the naive analysis led to erroneous findings due to measurement error bias, even when the regressor variables were assumed to be measured precisely. Root cause was a mix of one real code bug plus one auth-mode mismatch:

- Model probe failures always came back as generic “model not available”.

3. Your `copilot`/`github` probes are hitting GitHub Models endpoint (Azure URL)
- The 401 on `https://models.inference.ai.azure.com/chat/completions` indicates token/auth mismatch for GitHub Models.
- Copilot OAuth login is separate and applies to `copilot-oauth` provider, not `copilot`/`github` PAT-based paths.

Short answer: today, no, not effectively.

What that means:

- The top-level any-llm API accepts arbitrary extra arguments and forwards them:
  - [src/any_llm/api.py](../any-llm/src/any_llm/api.py#L22)
- The Copilot SDK provider receives those extras in kwargs:
  - [src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py](../any-llm/src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py#L345)
- But inside that provider, timeout is never read or enforced around:
  - non-streaming wait: [send_and_wait call](../any-llm/src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py#L392)
  - streaming loop: [queue wait loop](../any-llm/src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py#L332)

So timeout can be passed in, but the current copilotsdk provider implementation does not apply it. In practice, it behaves as unsupported/ignored for that provider.

If you want, I can patch any-llm so timeout is actually enforced for both non-streaming and streaming paths.

Yes. I’ll point you to the runtime paths already in this app and what they can/can’t discover for each provider type.Yes, with caveats.

Current runtime behavior in this app:

- Dynamic discovery exists for providers in scripts/web_app.py:
  - openai, anthropic, gemini, groq
- Static-only providers are in scripts/web_app.py:
  - copilot-oauth, copilot, github, local

How it works:

- Runtime discovery function: scripts/web_app.py
  - Calls any-llm list_models when API credentials are present.
- Results are cached in memory: scripts/web_app.py
- API endpoint to read catalog: scripts/routes/auth_routes.py

What this means for your question:

- For openai/anthropic/gemini/groq: yes, you can identify available models at runtime via the model catalog endpoint.
- For copilot-oauth/copylot/github: not true discovery yet. The app uses a static allowlist and then validates by probe-on-switch through scripts/routes/auth_routes.py.

Practical check you can do now:

- Call GET /api/model-catalog?providers=copilot-oauth
- You will get the configured allowlist for that provider, not a live discovery list.
- Then POST /api/model is the runtime truth test for each candidate model.

If you want, I can add a dedicated runtime probe endpoint that checks a list of candidate copilot-oauth models in one call and returns available vs unavailable.

# Copyright (C) 2026 Gregory R. Warnes
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later

"""Unit tests for model catalog helper discovery behavior."""

import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'scripts'))

from scripts.web_app import (
    _CATALOG_LIST_MODELS_CAPABLE,
    _catalog_anyllm_provider,
    _catalog_discover_provider_models,
)


class TestModelCatalogHelpers(unittest.TestCase):
    """Validate runtime model discovery helper behavior."""

    def test_catalog_marks_copilot_sdk_as_list_models_capable(self):
        """copilot-sdk should be eligible for runtime list_models discovery."""
        self.assertIn('copilot-sdk', _CATALOG_LIST_MODELS_CAPABLE)

    def test_catalog_maps_copilot_sdk_provider_name(self):
        """cv-builder provider key should map to any-llm provider slug."""
        self.assertEqual(_catalog_anyllm_provider('copilot-sdk'), 'copilotsdk')
        self.assertEqual(_catalog_anyllm_provider('openai'), 'openai')

    def test_copilot_sdk_discovery_does_not_require_api_key(self):
        """copilot-sdk list_models should run without token when CLI auth exists."""
        mock_list_models = MagicMock(
            return_value=[
                SimpleNamespace(id='gpt-4o'),
                SimpleNamespace(id='claude-3-7-sonnet'),
                SimpleNamespace(id='gpt-4o'),
            ]
        )

        with patch('scripts.web_app.os.getenv', return_value=None):
            with patch.dict('sys.modules', {'any_llm': SimpleNamespace(list_models=mock_list_models)}):
                models = _catalog_discover_provider_models('copilot-sdk')

        self.assertEqual(models, ['gpt-4o', 'claude-3-7-sonnet'])
        mock_list_models.assert_called_once_with(provider='copilotsdk')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

```

I finished the UI deprecation wiring and validated with a full JS test run plus bundle rebuild; next I’ll summarize exactly what is now deprecated in UI and what still remains functional in backend for compatibility.Yes, for the cv-builder LLM workflow, copilot-sdk supports the tasks you currently perform.

Why:
- It supports chat completions, which drive job analysis, recommendations, rewrite proposals, and other prompt-based flows via the shared LLM client methods.
- It supports list_models through any-llm (and we already wired runtime discovery for copilot-sdk in cv-builder).
- It does not support embeddings, but your core workflow does not require embeddings to function because semantic matching has non-embedding fallbacks in the shared client/orchestrator path.

Applied sections: Critical workflows, Multi-session architecture, When modifying code, and frontend bundle regeneration from `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Applied skills: copilot-preflight, cv-builder-patterns, workflow-orchestration.

I reproduced your 4 observations in code paths and shipped fixes for all four.

1. Copilot auth badge mismatch
- Root cause: the badge was not being refreshed from status payload during normal app status polling, so it could stay at stale "Not authenticated" even when server auth state was true.
- Fix: `web/api-client.js#L217` now syncs badge on every status fetch using copilot_auth + llm_provider, and updates global currentProvider.
- Extra sync on restore: `web/session-manager.js#L404` now updates the badge when restoring backend state.

2. "Reasoning…" and "Stop" visible while idle
- Root cause: inline LLM status bar could remain visible at idle.
- Fix: `web/fetch-utils.js#L148` now hides the inline bar and stop button when loading ends, and `web/fetch-utils.js#L213` routes setLoading through _updateLLMStatusBar so visibility is managed consistently.

3. Restored phase looked like Recommend Customizations without analysis
- Root cause: restored phase could be ahead of actual artifacts (phase persisted, analysis missing), so UI could land in analysis/customization actions incorrectly.
- Fix: `web/session-manager.js#L255` adds a restore-phase guard. If analysis is missing, restored phase is clamped to init before tab/action wiring at `web/session-manager.js#L467`.

4. Gemini rows remaining after selecting Copilot SDK and deselecting Gemini
- Root cause: provider toggles could race; if a refresh was in-flight, the next refresh request was dropped, leaving stale mixed-provider rows.
- Fix: `web/ui-core.js#L694` adds a pending-refresh queue flag so a second refresh reruns after the in-flight one completes. Also re-renders provider chips before table rebuild at `web/ui-core.js#L821`.

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="create_file"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **create_file**</summary>

**Input:**

- content:

```
// Copyright (C) 2026 Gregory R. Warnes
// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
//
// This file is part of CV-Builder.
// For commercial licensing, contact greg@warnes-innovations.com

/**
 * tests/js/setup.js
 * Global vitest setup: runs before every test file.
 *
 * 1. Provides a working in-memory localStorage stub.
 *    jsdom's built-in localStorage is unreliable in some worker
 *    configurations and causes "localStorage.setItem is not a function"
 *    errors in modules that call stateManager helpers.  Individual test
 *    files that need precise control (e.g. state-manager.test.js) call
 *    vi.stubGlobal('localStorage', ...) in their own beforeAll and
 *    override this stub.
 *
 * 2. Suppresses console.warn / console.error before each test.
 *    Production modules log expected error paths (network failures,
 *    invalid inputs, missing DOM elements) through the loglevel library
 *    which ultimately calls console.warn / console.error.  Tests assert
 *    on thrown exceptions and return values, not on log output.  The spy
 *    is re-applied in beforeEach so it survives any vi.restoreAllMocks()
 *    call made by individual test files.
 */

import { vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';

// ── 1. localStorage stub ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function createLocalStorageMock() {
  let store = {};
  return {
    getItem:    (key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(store, key) ? store[key] : null,
    setItem:    (key, value) => { store[key] = String(value); },
    removeItem: (key) => { delete store[key]; },
    clear:      () => { store = {}; },
    key:        (i) => Object.keys(store)[i] ?? null,
    get length() { return Object.keys(store).length; },
  };
}

// stubGlobal is not reset by vi.restoreAllMocks(), so this persists for the
// entire test file.  Individual files override it with vi.stubGlobal() in
// their own beforeAll if they need a different implementation.
vi.stubGlobal('localStorage', createLocalStorageMock());

// ── 2. Suppress production log output in tests ────────────────────────────────

// Re-applied in beforeEach so it survives vi.restoreAllMocks() calls in
// individual test files.
beforeEach(() => {
  vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
  vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
});

```

/**
 * tests/js/setup.js
 * Global vitest setup: runs before every test file.
 *
 * 1. Provides a working in-memory localStorage stub.

 *    invalid inputs, missing DOM elements) through the loglevel library
 *    which ultimately calls console.warn / console.error.  Tests assert
 *    on thrown exceptions and return values, not on log output.  The spy
 *    is re-applied in beforeEach so it survives any vi.restoreAllMocks()
 *    call made by individual test files.
 */

import { vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';

// ── 1. localStorage stub ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function createLocalStorageMock() {
  let store = {};
  return {
    getItem:    (key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(store, key) ? store[key] : null,
    setItem:    (key, value) => { store[key] = String(value); },
    removeItem: (key) => { delete store[key]; },
    clear:      () => { store = {}; },
    key:        (i) => Object.keys(store)[i] ?? null,
    get length() { return Object.keys(store).length; },
  };
}

fix(ui): resolve 4 LLM status and provider auth UI regressions

  call updateAuthBadge() on every status poll so the badge reflects the

  sign-in/sign-out actions

  display:none when loading is false, and setLoading() correctly routes
  through _updateLLMStatusBar instead of the floating overlay so the
  "Reasoning…" bar and Stop button disappear after each request
- Phase clamped on restore: _resolveRestoredPhase() resets to INIT when
  job_analysis data is absent, preventing the UI from landing on an
  action button that requires analysis it doesn't have
- Model catalog refresh queued: rapid provider checkbox toggles no longer
  drop the latest selection; _catalogRefreshPending queues one re-run so
  the table reflects the final toggle state

fix(backend): copilot-sdk provider wiring and probe error handling

- Map copilot-sdk to copilotsdk slug for any-llm API calls throughout
  web_app.py and llm_client.py
- Add copilot-sdk to _CATALOG_LIST_MODELS_CAPABLE so runtime model
  discovery runs for that provider
- _catalog_discover_provider_models skips api_key guard for copilot-sdk
  (uses CLI ambient auth) and passes correct provider slug to any-llm
- auth_routes: list_models_capable now driven by the canonical set rather
  than a hardcoded literal; probe error now returns the raw exception
  string so _format_probe_error can surface actionable auth guidance
- Clarify copilot-oauth vs github confusion in probe error messages

test: global vitest setup eliminates framework stderr noise

- Add tests/js/setup.js: global beforeEach stubs localStorage with a
  working in-memory mock, fixing "localStorage.setItem is not a function"
  across all test files that use stateManager helpers without their own stub
- vitest.config.mjs: add setupFiles and onConsoleLog(stderr→suppress) so
  loglevel's pre-bound console.warn/error calls don't leak into test output

  suppress the jsdom --localstorage-file Node process warning
- state-manager.test.js: re-asserts its own lsMock in beforeEach so the
  global setup stub doesn't shadow its controlled mock object
- Add tests/test_model_catalog_helpers.py: unit tests for catalog helper
  functions (_CATALOG_LIST_MODELS_CAPABLE, _catalog_anyllm_provider,
  copilot-sdk token-free discovery path)
